context.real_world_incident: Spring OXM (Object/XML Mapping) module's default configuration in Spring applications allowed XXE when unmarshalling XML to Java objects. This affected applications using RestTemplate with XML requests, custom XML parsing in services, and configuration file processing.
context.impact: Attackers can exploit XXE through any endpoint accepting XML input (REST APIs accepting XML, file uploads, configuration imports) to read files, perform SSRF attacks, cause denial of service, or extract data via blind XXE.
context.affected_versions: Spring OXM (all versions before patched), Spring Framework 3.0.0 - 3.2.3

references.description: Comprehensive XXE prevention guide with language-specific parser configuration

conversations.value: Our Spring Boot API needs to accept XML configuration files from users for importing settings. What's a safe way to handle XML parsing without introducing vulnerabilities?
How do we validate that XXE protections are working and handle legacy systems that need to accept external DTDs?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker uploads an XML configuration file containing external entity declarations. The application parses the uploaded XML to extract settings, but the parser resolves entities that read sensitive files (/etc/shadow, application.properties with database credentials) or make SSRF requests to internal services (cloud metadata endpoints at 169.254.169.254).
preconditions: Application accepts XML file uploads for configuration import
Uploaded XML is parsed with a parser that has external entities enabled
Application has network access to internal services or cloud metadata

secure_properties: XML parser factory configured to disable all external entity features
Uploaded files validated against strict XML Schema before parsing
File size limits prevent recursive entity expansion DoS
Alternative format (JSON/YAML) preferred over XML where possible
Network egress rules block requests to metadata endpoints
negative_properties: Must not parse uploaded XML with default parser settings
Must not allow DOCTYPE declarations in imported configuration files
Must not process XML parameter entities from untrusted sources
Must not give application access to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254)
